title: MQSA quality standards
summary: The federal rules that shape everyday mammography work: certification and accreditation, technologist qualifications, reports and results timelines, labeling, records, the outcomes audit, required policies, and equipment QC basics.

visuals.title: Where does the view and laterality marker go?
visuals.prompt: On this schematic MLO, select the region where MQSA requires the view and laterality label.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Region B, right side near the outer contour
Region D, center of the image
hotspots.revealLabel: Over breast tissue: would obscure anatomy

feedback.a: Correct. View and laterality go near the axilla, using standardized codes.
feedback.b: Not here. The regulation places view and laterality near the axilla, not the nipple.
feedback.c: Not here. This is away from the axilla; the required position is near the axilla.
feedback.d: Not here. A label over breast tissue would obscure anatomy, which no label may do.

visuals.explanation: § 900.12(c)(5)(iii) places view and laterality near the axilla. All labels must be permanent, legible, unambiguous, and must not obscure anatomic structures.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Each region can be chosen with the keyboard or a screen reader using its position description. The positions describe the same information a sighted learner sees; recognizing which position corresponds to the axilla is the skill being tested.

visuals.title: Components along the beam path
visuals.prompt: Select the beam-limiting device on this schematic unit.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Component A, top of the C-arm
Component C, thin plate above the breast
Component D, base below the breast

feedback.a: That's the tube housing assembly, where x-rays are produced. The beam-limiting device sits just below it to shape the field.
feedback.b: Correct. The beam-limiting device shapes the x-ray field between the tube and the patient.
feedback.c: That's the compression paddle. It contacts the breast; it doesn't limit the beam.
feedback.d: That's the breast support containing the image receptor.

visuals.explanation: MQSA defines a mammography unit as including at least an x-ray generator, x-ray control, tube housing assembly, beam-limiting device, and supporting structures (§ 900.2(dd)). Along the beam: tube housing → beam-limiting device → compression paddle → breast → breast support and receptor.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Components are described by position only; their names appear after you answer.

visuals.title: Results deadline on a timeline
visuals.prompt: A screening exam on day 0 is assessed Benign. Select the latest day by which the patient's lay summary must be provided.

hotspots.revealLabel: Day 7: deadline for Suspicious/Highly Suggestive (from final interpretation)
Day 30: lay summary and provider report deadline
Day 60: not an MQSA results deadline

feedback.a: 7 days applies to Suspicious or Highly Suggestive results, counted from the final interpretation.
feedback.b: 15 days is the deadline for transferring records after a request.
feedback.c: Correct. Lay summaries are due within 30 calendar days of the exam.
feedback.d: Too late. The lay summary is due within 30 calendar days.

visuals.explanation: Lay summary: within 30 calendar days of the exam, or within 7 calendar days of final interpretation for Suspicious or Highly Suggestive results.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Markers are announced by day number. This exercise is fully equivalent in text form.

visuals.title: Where does 'dense' begin?
visuals.prompt: Select the least dense category whose lay summary must say 'Your breast tissue is dense.'

hotspots.revealLabel: Dense: first category requiring the dense statement

feedback.a: Almost entirely fatty maps to 'not dense.'
feedback.b: Scattered fibroglandular density still maps to 'not dense.'
feedback.c: Correct. Heterogeneously dense is the lower of the two categories that receive the dense statement.
feedback.d: Extremely dense receives the dense statement, but it isn't the least dense category that does.

visuals.explanation: The first two report categories map to 'not dense'; heterogeneously and extremely dense map to 'dense' (§ 900.12(c)(2)(iii)–(iv)).
visuals.accessibilityNote: Category names are read aloud because they are printed on the image; the dense/not-dense mapping is revealed only after you answer.

glossary.definition: An entity approved by FDA to accredit mammography facilities.
Minimum and maximum values of a QA measurement representing acceptable performance; values outside them require corrective action.
An undesirable experience associated with mammography, such as poor image quality, late reports, or use of unqualified personnel.
Approval of a facility by FDA or a State certification agency to provide mammography services.
Anyone commenting on or complaining about a mammography exam, including the patient or a representative such as a family member or referring provider.
An hour of training received through direct instruction. One continuing education unit equals one contact hour.
For an exam, the supervisor is present to observe and correct the person performing it.
Enhancing Quality Using the Inspection Program: FDA inspection questions on ongoing clinical image quality, corrective action, and lead interpreting physician oversight of QA records.
The interpreting physician with general responsibility for the facility's QA program.
A breast radiography technology such as screen-film, FFDM, or DBT.
An onsite assessment by a medical physicist after installation, reassembly, or major repair, before clinical use.
A mammogram assessed Suspicious or Highly Suggestive of Malignancy.
A certificate of up to 6 months that lets a new facility perform mammography while completing accreditation; one 90-day extension possible.
A qualified technologist responsible for QA tasks not assigned to the lead interpreting physician or medical physicist.
Percentage of screening mammograms assessed 'Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation.'
A report of a serious adverse event.
A 4.2 cm compressed breast of 50% glandular and 50% adipose tissue, used for phantom dosimetry.
